final_message:
I built the Ploverdesk landing page, but I couldn't run `npm run build`: this sandbox has no Node binary (`npm` is blocked and there's no `node` on PATH). TypeScript and Vite have not checked the code, and I never saw the page rendered.

### What's on the page

- **First screen:** the headline "Only the invoice lines that don't match reach your desk.", a short explanation, the "Start the 14-day trial" button (to `/trial`), "No credit card", and a quieter "book a demo" link (to `/demo`).
- **The example invoice:** under that sits a table showing one supplier invoice after the three-way match. Three lines match and are shown in grey with a ✓. Three don't, and stay in black with the wrong value in red:
  - 4 corner boards invoiced but not delivered;
  - a unit price 5.00 above the purchase order;
  - a tape dispenser that never arrived.

  The table is captioned "Illustrative lines, not customer data." On phones each line becomes a small block with every value labelled.
- **The terms:** 290 EUR per month per company, no limit on users, export as a CSV file or through an API, data in Frankfurt, a 14-day trial with no credit card.
- **Who builds it:** founded in 2025, six people in Rotterdam. It says plainly that there are no customer logos yet, then repeats the trial button. A footer follows.
- **Style:** white, near-black and grey, with one red used only for a mismatch, never on buttons, links or headings. Flat and sharp-cornered with thin rules, no shadows, gradients or images. The type is the system font with figures aligned in columns. I left out a web font, partly because no network was available. I'd also keep it that way: a Google Fonts request would send each visitor's IP outside the EU, which undercuts the Frankfurt hosting point.
- **Motion:** the one animation is the match itself. Shortly after the page loads, the matched lines fade from black to grey in turn and the mismatches stay. If the animation doesn't run, or reduced motion is on, the table already sits in that final state. Hovers are quick colour or underline changes; nothing moves on scroll.
- **Invented content:** no logos, testimonials or usage numbers. The only figures I made up are the example invoice's quantities and prices, which are labelled as illustrative. If the founders want no invented figures at all, those are the ones to replace.

### Files

- `index.html`: title and description.
- `src/App.tsx`: the page.
- `src/index.css`: page styles.
- `src/tokens.css`: colours, type, spacing and timing values.
- `MASTER.md`: the design system and the reasoning behind it.
- `preview/thesis.html` and `preview/design-system.html`: throwaway previews, not used by the build.

### Decisions I made alone

Nobody was available, so the design direction and the design system are my own calls and **not approved**. Both are written out in full in `MASTER.md`. I also assumed English copy, light mode only, and no dark mode.

### What I checked by reading the code

- **Contrast:** computed from the colour values, all pass. Body text 18.0:1, grey 6.1:1, red 6.6:1, grey on the terms band 5.6:1, button-text on hover 13.5:1.
- **Reduced motion:** there's a rule that removes the animation and transitions.
- **Keyboard focus:** a visible outline on the wordmark, buttons and links; the outline is never removed.
- **Mobile:** the header and hero links meet the 44px tap-target minimum, and hover styles only apply on devices with a mouse.
- **Hard-coded values:** none beyond two breakpoints and a standard hidden-text helper.
- **Audit script:** clean, apart from one "hover with no transition" finding that's wrong — the transitions are on the base styles.
- **First screen:** my reading showed the last example line falling below the fold on a 1440×800 screen. I widened the headline and tightened two gaps, and by my arithmetic it now fits (about 776px of 800). That is an estimate, not a measurement.
- **Two deliberate patterns:** thin rules on every table row, and the example table standing in for the product. The audit counts both as "AI reflexes" because no one approved the design. I kept them on purpose.

### Still to run yourself

| Check | How | Should see |
|---|---|---|
| Build | `npm run build` | type-check and build pass |
| Widths | open the page at 375, 768, 1024 and 1440px | no sideways scroll, nothing cut off; at 1440×800 all six example lines visible before scrolling |
| Animation smoothness | Chrome DevTools > Performance, recorded on page load | no frame over 16.7ms |
| Reduced motion | turn on "reduce motion" in the OS, then reload | the table appears already settled, nothing animates |
| Screen reader | on a phone width | the example table still reads as a table |

On process:
- A larger multi-agent site pipeline (bunshin) exists, but it targets multi-page sites, and this brief is one page.
- The modules loaded were motion-principles, css-native, mobile-principles, tells, ui-ux-pro-max and design-audit.
- About 1.5k characters from the middle of mobile-principles were cut off when it was displayed to me; the parts I relied on came through whole.
